title: Compatible roots of unity and the prime-to-p product of adic integers
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] of characteristic $p>0$. For a positive integer $m$ prime to $p$, put $\mu_m(k)=\{z\in k^\times:z^m=1\}$, with its discrete topology. There exists a family of primitive roots $\zeta_m\in\mu_m(k)$ (each $\zeta_m$ has multiplicative order exactly $m$) for all such $m$ with $\zeta_1=1$ and $\zeta_n^{n/m}=\zeta_m$ whenever $m\mid n$. For any such family, the maps $\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z\to\mu_m(k)$, $a\mapsto\zeta_m^a$, induce an isomorphism of topological groups
$$
\varprojlim_{(m,p)=1}\mu_m(k)\cong\prod_{r\text{ prime},\ r\ne p}(\mathbf Z_r,+),
$$
where the transition from $\mu_n(k)$ to $\mu_m(k)$ is $z\mapsto z^{n/m}$, the inverse limit and product have their standard inverse-limit and product topologies, and $\mathbf Z_r$ is the ring of adic integers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], identified topologically with $\varprojlim_{a\ge1}\mathbf Z/r^a\mathbf Z$. The isomorphism is allowed to depend on the family of primitive roots.

proof.text: For each positive tame order m, take the finite nonempty set of primitive m-th roots, using [lem-sc-primitive-root]. Order the tame integers by divisibility, directed by multiplication. For m dividing n send z to z^(n/m); exact order follows from cancellation, identities from m/m=1, and composition from (N/n)(n/m)=N/m. Apply the finite nonempty cofiltered-system section theorem [lem-trf-cofiltered-finite-sets-section]. The section supplies all compatible primitive roots, and the order-one root equation gives normalization. No surjectivity of transitions or recursive primitive-root lifting is needed.

Fix any compatible primitive family. Use the finite cyclic trivializations from [lem-sc-primitive-root], concretely IsPrimitiveRoot.zmodAddEquivRootsOfUnity. Their values are zeta_m raised to the canonical representative of a residue. Compatibility of the family and reduction of exponents modulo m show that these trivializations intertwine power transitions with residue reductions. Apply them coordinatewise to give an additive-to-multiplicative group isomorphism between the subring of compatible residues and the root limit. Injectivity and surjectivity follow coordinatewise from the finite equivalences.

For m>0 use ZMod.equivPi, the integer-residue specialization of [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product], to reconstruct a residue modulo m from its prime-power coordinates. Evaluate each input adic integer at the exponent v_r(m). Ring homomorphisms out of ZMod are unique, so each CRT projection is the canonical reduction. Compatibility of the adic residue maps from [lem-exc-padic-residue-universal-property] then proves the reconstruction is compatible under divisibility. At exponent zero the target ZMod 1 is a singleton, and CRT at m=1 is the empty product.

Conversely, restrict a compatible tame residue family to each prime-power order and apply PadicInt.lift from [lem-exc-padic-residue-universal-property]. Its lift_spec gives every residue of the resulting adic integer. CRT injectivity proves reconstruction after restriction is the identity, and separation by all adic residues proves restriction after reconstruction is the identity. Thus reconstruction is a bijective ring homomorphism from the adic product to compatible residues.

Compose reconstruction with the root trivializations. Each output coordinate factors through finitely many adic residue maps and a map between discrete spaces. The kernel and norm description in [lem-exc-padic-residue-universal-property] makes each residue map continuous: a norm ball of radius r^(-a) lies in its fibre. In Lean use the existing proved PadicInt.continuous_toZModPow. Hence the composite into the initial root-limit topology is continuous. The adic integers are compact by Mathlib.NumberTheory.Padics.ProperSpace, and their product is compact. The root limit embeds continuously and injectively in the product of discrete unit groups, hence is Hausdorff. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-compact-hausdorff-bijection] to obtain continuity of the inverse.

Take the inverse topological group equivalence. Applying the forward inverse law at a prime-power order identifies the given root coordinate with its primitive root raised to the CRT residue. The prime-power specification of CRT reconstruction identifies that residue with PadicInt.toZModPow of the corresponding product coordinate. This proves exactly the required displayed normalization, also for a=0 and m=1.

proof_origin.place: Second paragraph, tame product. Finite inverse-system compactness replaces recursive generator lifting; explicit CRT and PadicInt.lift give both inverse laws; compact-to-Hausdorff gives inverse continuity.
